title: Traffic containment + autorestore UX sketches
content:
Overview:
This doc captures lightweight UX sketches and operator flows for two linked features: 1) traffic containment (fast, surgical reductions in traffic to a variant when health signals degrade) and 2) autorestore (automated progressive re-introduction of previously contained variants once they meet health criteria). Goal is to reduce toil during incidents and make automatic fallback behavior visible, configurable, and predictable for platform users.

Context / Motivation:
- Operators currently set canary windows and manual rollbacks; during transient infra blips this leads to noisy rollbacks and follow-up manual restores.
- We need a way to contain noisy variants quickly (minimize blast radius) while capturing enough signals to either fully roll back or safely reintroduce.
- Console must show what happened, why, and offer clear next actions (investigate, pin, rollback, hold, schedule reintroduce).

High-level goals:
- Fast containment: let operator reduce a variant to 0% (or to a containment floor) in one click with pre-defined guardrails.
- Explainability: show the trigger that caused containment (metrics, recent errors, infra events).
- Autorestore: allow system to attempt progressive reintroduce according to a policy (time-window, step sizes, and health checks) or explicitly schedule it.
- Safety hooks: require approval for autorestore for enterprise customers, allow automatic autorestore for lower tiers.

Personas:
- Platform engineer (owner of Redwood Dedicated tenant) — cares about SLOs, wants minimal human intervention during off-hours.
- Product engineer (uses hosted API) — wants visibility into model regressions and simple rollback/restore controls.
- On-call SRE — needs immediate containment, rich telemetry, and one-click runbook links.

Primary flows (sketch-level):
1) Detection -> Contain flow (fast path for on-call)
   - Detection: alert triggers (error rate spike, latency outlier, model quality regression from evals).
   - Inline action in alert or from Rollouts page: "Contain variant" CTA.
   - Modal: quick summary of why (top metrics), recommended containment floor (0% or 5%), suggested duration (default 30m), and downstream impacts (estimated reduced throughput).
   - Confirm -> timeline annotated with an immediate containment event.
   - Telemetry: containment event logs with actor, reason, and signal snapshot.

2) Containment -> Investigate -> Decide
   - Left rail: list of active rollouts with small status chips (Healthy / Contained / Degraded).
   - Center panel: variant timeline, colored bars for traffic percentage, markers for containment events, hover to see snapshots.
   - Right panel: health summary and diagnostic tabs (metrics, logs link, recent prompts/evals).
   - Operator can: pin a stable variant, escalate to full rollback, or schedule autorestore.

3) Autorestore (policy-driven progressive reintroduce)
   - Policy composer: simple UI to build autorestore policies. Options: enable/disable; max step size (e.g., +10% every 15m), health checks (error rate, p50/p95 latency, quality regression threshold), max attempts, and cool-down.
   - Preview simulation: small sandbox run to show projected traffic timeline and guard conditions that would abort reintroduce.
   - Execution: when policy is active the system charts each step and pauses if a check fails. All steps are recorded and reversible.

Wireframe notes (visual layout):
- Header: Rollout name, environment tag, primary CTA cluster (Contain, Rollback, Promote, Edit policy).
- Left rail: compact variants list w/ miniature sparkline and status badge. Click variant focuses center timeline.
- Center: timeline + traffic slider with play/pause for autorestore simulation. Timeline rows per variant, stacked traffic view. Containment events appear as red flags; autorestore steps as green ticks.
- Right: health panel with quick metrics and deep links. Tabs: Metrics (timeseries), Alerts (related alerts), Eval snapshots (recent prompt set pass/fail), Logs (link), Runbook (link to Confluence).
- Modal patterns: quick-contain (fast minimal form), advanced-contain (choose retention floor, auto-notify, slack routing).

Microcopy suggestions:
- Contain CTA: "Contain variant — stop routing to this version" 
- Confirm modal line: "This will route X% -> Y% (estimated requests/day). Alerts and webhooks will be fired. You can schedule autorestore after containment."
- Autorestore policy rule: "If error-rate <= 0.5% and p95 < 1.5s for 15m, increase traffic by 10% every 15m up to prior baseline."

Acceptance criteria (grooming-ready):
- UX: Contain flows reachable from both Rollout list and alert details; quick contain modal implemented.
- Policy: Autorestore composer with fields for step-size, interval, health checks, and max attempts.
- Telemetry: every containment/autorestore step emits event w/ actor, timestamp, metrics snapshot, and reason.
- Visibility: timeline renders containment and autorestore events; hovering shows metric snapshots.
- Safety: autorestore can be gated by required-approval flag per org.

Backlog items (candidate tickets):
- PLAT-4890: implement containment API endpoint + audit events (owner: Marcus P)
- INFR-3421: circuit-breaker metric hooks and alert payload changes (owner: SRE team)
- UX-775: wireframe and microcopy for quick-contain modal (owner: Lina R)
- CONSOLE-203: timeline component with containment/restore markers + hover snapshot (owner: frontend team)
- QA-1122: end-to-end test for autorestore policy abort conditions

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- How aggressive should default autorestore steps be? (conservative by default, opt-in progressive aggressive for canary experiments)
- Should containment be reversible only via autorestore or allow manual percent adjustments? (allow both)
- Where to store policy defaults? Org-level, project-level, or per-rollout? (pref: org-level with per-rollout override)
- Compliance: for Private deployments, customers may require approval for any autorestore — need settings surfaced in onboarding.

Telemetry & observability requirements (minimal):
- Event types: containment.requested, containment.executed, autorestore.step_start, autorestore.step_end, autorestore.abort, policy.update.
- Exposed metrics for dashboards: mean time to contain, mean time to restore, containment frequency by variant, autorestore success rate.

Runbook / playbook snippets (for on-call):
- If containment was triggered by infra blip, mark containment as "investigating" and wait 10m for infra alerts to clear. If no infra alert but model-quality regression, escalate to ML owner.
- Use "preview simulation" before enabling autorestore for controversial models.

Next steps (immediate):
- UX: mock quick-contain modal + timeline annotation (Lina) — due 2025-12-10
- Backend: containment API + audit events spec (Marcus) — due 2025-12-15
- SRE: adjust alerting to include containment CTA links (Ethan) — due 2025-12-18
- Sync: cross-team grooming session (30m) to align on default policy values — schedule week of 2025-12-01

Notes / references:
- Related design doc: confluence:/ui/rollouts/designs (see section "containment patterns")
- Linked PR prototype for timeline: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/512
- Slack thread with early signals + requirements: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C01234567/p1700000000000000

Quick thought: labeling containment states with human-friendly reasons (e.g., "High p95 latency" vs raw metric values) drastically reduces triage time. Consider a short auto-generated sentence for every containment event.

Owner and reviewers:
- Owner: Ava Chen (product-console)
- Reviewers: Marcus Patel (platform), Lina Rodriguez (UX), Ethan Cole (SRE)

Status: draft — looking for feedback on the policy composer fields and suggested default values.
